👋 Hey, I'm Praveen! I'm a first-year PhD student in Computer Science at Brown University, and I'm interested in the responsible use of algorithmic decisions in society, using methods in ML, statistics, and the social sciences.

praveen_nair@brown.edu • CV • Google Scholar • GitHub • LinkedIn

At Brown 🐻, I’m working with Professor Suresh Venkatasubramanian at the Center for Technological Responsibility, Reimagination, and Redesign (CNTR). Currently, we’re studying how high-stakes decisionmaking models can be monitored in messy, post-deployment contexts where labels are scarce, from both a theoretical and practical standpoint.

As an RA with Professor Amit Goldenberg at Harvard Business School, I contributed to a number of projects dealing with AI and emotional support. This included the implementation, management, and analysis of an interactive study on AI vs. human performance in cognitive reappraisal tasks (preprint here).

In 2024, I graduated from UC San Diego 🔱 with a master’s in computer science, where I was advised by Professor David Danks. My thesis uses causal inference and active learning to study fairness-sensitive decisions with selective labeling, establishing how even without biased or flawed models, imbalances in group size can lead to differences in uncertainty.

At UCSD, I was also a teaching assistant supervising the data science capstone course and DSC 80. Prior to my graduate study, I was a data science major at UC San Diego, graduating with minors in history and liguistics, and a concentration in political science. Outside the classroom, I was the sports editor of The UCSD Guardian, was in UCSD’s quizbowl club, and spent a summer making a documentary about UCSD’s history. In my free time, I’m watching a lot of sports ⚾️, reading Wikipedia, and watching movies.

🧑‍💻 Research Interests

  • Responsible ML: Can we responsibly deploy algorithmic decisionmaking systems into messy, dynamic real-world contexts effectively? What best practices for developers, auditors, or regulators do we need to prevent deployment-time failures?

  • Causal inference: How can we integrate causal information across datasets to improve scientific discovery? Can the abstractions of causation give us the tools to develop more responsible ML systems?

  • Human-AI Interaction: How do the ways in which humans perceive and react to algorithmic systems affect the way in which we should design them?
